answers.question: What was the task?
answers.answer: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows milliseconds.
quotes: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows milliseconds.

answers.question: How did it end: what is done and what is not?
answers.answer: The rename is done in the code and in our settings file and both tests pass, but the operations team's production file still uses the old name.
quotes: That is done in the code and in our settings file, and both tests pass.
One thing is left. The operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name.

answers.question: How does the thing that changed work?
answers.answer: The code reads only the new name, falls back to five seconds when it is missing, and our settings file gives three seconds under the new name.
quotes: The code now reads only the new name. When the name is missing, it falls back to five seconds. Our settings file gives three seconds under the new name.

answers.question: What is the problem, and what causes it?
answers.answer: The production file sets the timeout under the old name, which the code no longer reads, so production waits three seconds instead of ten after the release.
quotes: The code no longer reads that name, so after the release production waits three seconds instead of ten.
The operations file sets ten seconds under the old name. Nobody reads that name now. So production gets our three seconds.

answers.question: What is not verified?
answers.answer: The tests do not read the production file, and the author did not see the loading of the files in production, only a comment in the code saying the operations file goes on top of ours.
quotes: They do not read the production file.
I know this from a comment in the code; I did not see the loading itself.

answers.question: What do I have to decide, and what does each option give and cost?
answers.missing: The text would have to name the decision the reader takes (for example who updates the production file and when, or whether the release waits) and say what each option gives and costs; it says only that the file was left alone because changes go through operations.
